question.text: A train with cross-sectional area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></math> is moving with speed <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></math> inside a long tunnel of cross-sectional area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mfenced></math>. Assume that almost all the air (density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ρ</mi></math>) in front of the train flows back between its sides and the walls of the tunnel. Also, the airflow with respect to the train is steady and laminar. Take the ambient pressure and that inside the train to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math>. If the pressure in the region between the sides of the train and the tunnel walls is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>-</mo><mi>P</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>7</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>N</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>ρ</mi><msubsup><mi>v</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi></math> is _______.
